item.title: Airline Sentiment Analysis: Interactive Exploration with Streamlit
item.description:
Executive summary

This case study describes an interactive Streamlit app for exploring tweets about airlines, grouped by positive, negative and neutral sentiment. Users can inspect sentiment distributions, filter by time and location, compare airlines and explore frequently used terms.

The project focuses on exploratory analysis and visualization of sentiment-labeled tweets. The original article does not document training or evaluating a new sentiment classification model. Its use of a tweet dataset should not be confused with verified real-time social media ingestion.

item.title: Sales and Returns Analytics: Building a Power BI Dashboard
item.description:
Executive summary

This project explores a Power BI dashboard for sales and product returns at a fictional electronics retail chain. The solution transforms XLSX source files with Power Query and organizes three complementary analytical views: overall performance, product and brand performance, and returns.

The objective is to make business indicators easier to explore and support discussions about commercial performance and operational improvements. The project is a portfolio case study; it does not report production adoption or independently measured savings.

item.title: Boutique Manager: Automating Retail Operations with Bash
item.description:
Executive summary

Boutique Manager is a shell scripting project for a small clothing shop scenario. Its command-line menu brings together product registration, inventory updates, sales, stock alerts, reporting, logging and backups.

The project originated from applying concepts studied in the Hands-on Introduction to Linux Commands and Shell Scripting course. It is a practical automation exercise, rather than a claim of deployment at a commercial retailer.

item.title: Building a Python ETL Pipeline: Unifying CSV, JSON and XML Data
item.description:
Executive summary

This project demonstrates a straightforward Extract, Transform, Load (ETL) workflow written in Python. It consolidates records stored in CSV, JSON and XML files into a consistent dataset and produces two artifacts: transformed_data.csv and log_file.txt.

The case study focuses on the core engineering considerations behind the implementation: heterogeneous inputs, standardization rules, repeatable execution and traceability through logs. It is a small-scale educational pipeline, rather than a production platform.
